tools.description: WRITE-ONCE: do NOT call this tool with empty or placeholder arguments to probe or discover its schema — the required `body` field is listed in this schema; if you are not ready to post a real comment, call `noop` instead. Adds a comment to an existing GitHub issue, pull request, or discussion. Use this to provide feedback, answer questions, or add information to an existing conversation. For creating new items, use create_issue, create_discussion, or create_pull_request instead. IMPORTANT: Comments are subject to validation constraints enforced by the MCP server - maximum 65536 characters for the complete comment (including footer which is added automatically), 10 mentions (@username), and 50 links. Exceeding these limits will result in an immediate error with specific guidance. NOTE: Discussion comments are disabled for this workflow because discussions:write permission is not available. Set 'discussions: true' in the workflow's safe-outputs.add-comment configuration to enable discussion comments and request this permission. CONSTRAINTS: Maximum 2 comment(s) can be added. Target: 648. This tool records a real comment intent. Do not use it for placeholder comments, auth checks, or probing. Call it only when the final comment body is ready; otherwise use noop or report_incomplete.

body.description: The comment text in Markdown format. Must be the final intended comment — not a placeholder or test value. This is the 'body' field - do not use 'comment_body' or other variations. Provide helpful, relevant information that adds value to the conversation. CONSTRAINTS: The complete comment (your body text + automatically added footer) must not exceed 65536 characters total. Maximum 10 mentions (@username), maximum 50 links (http/https URLs). A footer (~200-500 characters) is automatically appended with workflow attribution, so leave adequate space. If these limits are exceeded, the tool call will fail with a detailed error message indicating which constraint was violated.

comment_id.description: Existing issue or pull request comment ID to update instead of creating a new comment.

integrity.description: Trustworthiness level of the message source (e.g., "low", "medium", "high").

item_number.description: The issue, pull request, or discussion number to comment on. This is the numeric ID from the GitHub URL (e.g., 123 in github.com/owner/repo/issues/123). Can also be a temporary_id from a previously created issue in the same workflow run — use the '#aw_abc123' form; the bare 'aw_abc123' form is also accepted and normalised to '#aw_abc123'. If omitted, the tool auto-targets the issue, PR, or discussion that triggered this workflow. Auto-targeting only works for issue, pull_request, discussion, and comment event triggers — it does NOT work for schedule, workflow_dispatch, push, or workflow_run triggers. For those trigger types, always provide item_number explicitly, or the tool call will fail with an error. Required when safe-outputs.add-comment.target is '*' (any item): calls without item_number (or pr_number/pr alias) are rejected. NOTE: this field is named item_number, NOT issue_number.

pr.description: Alias for item_number when targeting a pull request. Prefer item_number in new calls.

arguments.body:
Updates the "Histograms in delta temporality only" limitation in `docs/reference/compatibility/limitations.md`, which stated a blanket delta-only restriction for histograms. The restriction has been renamed and scoped: both delta and cumulative temporality are now supported for histograms and counters via the Elasticsearch OTLP endpoint (`motlp`) on Elastic Stack 9.5+ and serverless, while the collector's Elasticsearch exporter path still only supports delta temporality for histograms.

**Triage rationale:** The issue provided clear before/after technical claims (what changed, the caveat that the collector exporter path is unaffected, and the exact section/lines to update), verifiable against the linked `docs-content://manage-data/ingest/otlp-endpoint.md#metric-temporality` page referenced elsewhere in this same file. This made the change sufficiently specified for autonomous handling without needing to guess at unstated product behavior.

**Drafting sources**
- Elastic Docs Contribution guide and cumulative-docs/`applies_to` guidelines (fetched conceptually via repository conventions; existing `applies_to` usage in `docs/reference/compatibility/limitations.md` frontmatter and other pages in `docs/reference/compatibility/`)
- Existing published page: `docs/reference/compatibility/limitations.md` (source of the change)
- Linked implementation/reference: `docs-content://manage-data/ingest/otlp-endpoint.md#metric-temporality` (Metric temporality docs referenced in the issue)
- Issue #648 body, including the specific proposed wording, line range, and applies_to guidance from the reporter

**Reader test**
- Reader goal: an Elastic Observability user configuring OTel metric ingestion, determining whether cumulative-temporality histograms/counters are supported and what's required, depending on ingestion path (ES OTLP endpoint vs. collector ES exporter).
- Rounds: 2
- Round 1 found one blocking gap: the draft didn't clarify that the collector-exporter delta-only restriction never applied to counters, only histograms, which could have left readers uncertain about counter behavior on that path.
- Round 2 (after adding "This restriction doesn't apply to counters."): no blocking comprehension gaps remained.

Related to #648
